chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a group of the Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him to appoint them over the charities of the livestock, saying, 'Let this portion which Allah has made for the workers upon it be for us, for we are more deserving of it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'O sons of Abdul Muttalib! Indeed, charity is not permissible for me nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, he (peace be upon him and his family) has indeed been promised it. So what is your opinion, O sons of Abdul Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise? Do you see me giving preference to others over you?'

key_terms.السَّهْمُ: The portion (specifically the share of the collector)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Banu Hashim ask to collect charity and what was the Prophet's response regarding their eligibility?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between the general prohibition of sadaqah for the Prophet and his family (Banu Hashim) and the specific exception of the 'portion of the collector' (al-sahm al-amil), which they could claim as workers. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links this material privilege to the spiritual promise of intercession (shafa'ah), emphasizing that the Prophet’s priority for his family in Paradise is a certainty derived from divine promise. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Ahl al-Bayt’s exclusion from general charity does not diminish their unique status or their right to specific allocations.
